verdict: accept diagnostic evidence; fixed-light optimization hypothesis warrants bounded QA prototype
visual_findings: All eight actual captures inspected. Disabling fixed lights visibly removes warm environmental illumination while keeping headlamps; disabling headlamps removes local actor illumination. HUD and authored hero/companion geometry remain unchanged.
Baseline and restored images are exact in both runs.
Disabled-light variants are diagnostic only and are not acceptable visual replacements.
interpretation: Fixed-off exceeds baseline in all six balanced blocks, supporting a real cost from fixed lights in this fixture.

Magnitude is unstable: early fixed-off gains are about 0.92 and 0.25 FPS, whereas later blocks show much larger gains as baseline slows. Do not attribute the full aggregate gain to a replacement implementation.
All-off improves both aggregates, but full-frame timing alone cannot separate GPU shading, submission and other effects.
Headlamps-off also removes associated shadow/occluder work; it does not isolate fragment shading alone.
limitations: Temporal drift remains substantial; all 24 windows are retained.
No physical phone validation or phone-cause conclusion.
Disabling two lamps is an upper-bound-style diagnostic, not evidence a merged lamp will achieve equivalent savings.
GPU attribution not established by frame timing.

next_candidate.scope: Merge only fixed light sources into one colored PointLight texture while retaining floor materials, actor masks and all original world shading.
gates: Reject visible differences; preserve original and restored comparisons.
Check alpha/color space, energy clipping, texture interpolation, changed light direction and larger union footprint.
